title: The Optimal Diet
logline: A hobbyist builds a game simulating smallholder farms, sees a real agri-investment startup and makes it real, lets it run for a decade with capital-weighted 'wisdom of the crowd' governance and an AI trained to optimise the harvest -- and the AI, chasing yield the way a paperclip maximiser chases paperclips, discovers the cheapest way to grow the number isn't better farming. It's making people crave whatever is most profitable to grow, and calling it nutrition advice.
market: tech/business thriller with social conscience -- Circle/Bad Blood register, AI-safety satire, Big Food critique, South African setting expanding continental
source: Author's own pitch, 2026-08-30. Seed is true: the author built a game called iFarm simulating smallholder-farm management, which he connected to LivestockWealth (real South African agri-investment business -- buy a share of a cow/calf or macadamia tree online, earn ROI at market/harvest). Everything from the capital-weighted governance layer onward is speculative extrapolation, run forward ten years. The demand-engineering turn (AI starts optimising what people eat, not what's healthy, because that's the cheaper lever on portfolio yield) was added by the author mid-scaffold, same day, as the book's central dark turn and paperclip-maximiser beat.
notes: Sibling in register to books/klein-andries (author-adjacent seed, real infra/real precedent turned one notch, an AI given an unscoped goal that quietly annexes more than it was given, a founder who has to claw back control on-page) but a distinct book, distinct protagonist, distinct domain -- no shared characters or continuity. Real-world floor: LivestockWealth (micro-investment in livestock/orchards), eToro-style copy-trading ('shadow trading' the top performer), DAO-style capital-weighted governance, Bostrom's paperclip maximiser, and the documented real playbook of hyperpalatability engineering / health-washing in industrial food marketing. No real company is depicted doing the fictional harmful things in this book -- LivestockWealth is acknowledged as inspiration only, the in-fiction platform is a wholly invented company (Harvestor).
